We demonstrate that for a genus-two fully twisted Veech curve, a  real-analytic family of Hitchin representations, which we prove to be a complete family, exists and enables the construction of a unitary Hitchin connection, thereby proving the polynomial boundedness of its holomorphic sections' coefficients in terms of a suitable norm on the curve's moduli space. This, in turn, allows the extension of a previously known representation, which was initially differentially-covariant on a rational flat surface, now as a Hitchin representation, and we leverage this connection to establish almost optimal bounds on the Laplacian eigenvalue spacing within a nearby genus-two hyperbolic surface family.

This study assesses the effectiveness of remote work on the performance of software projects utilizing Scrum methodology.  The evaluation is based on lessons learned from the significant shift to remote work during the COVID-19 pandemic.  To provide a comprehensive evaluation, we combined quantitative and qualitative methodologies in our evaluation framework.  The results highlight that working Scrum projects from home can be successful, but they demand more effort to establish and maintain productivity compared to in-person collaborations.  Key areas that need attention when Scrum projects are conducted remotely include setting up efficient videoconferencing tools, fostering strong team bonds, and ensuring effective communication.  To facilitate this, our research proposes the adoption of a distributed Scrum Master to support remote teams in their transition to successful remote work.

The concept of dichotomous matrices, introduced by R. E. Gaun and Y. C. Wu, involves analyzing matrices through a combination of ones and zeros, along with arbitrary coefficients. This has led to various studies investigating whether certain matrix types can be represented as dichotomous matrices, with numerous discoveries made in recent years. This paper builds upon previous work, specifically determining the maximum number of ones in a specific class of $4 \times 4$ matrices and matrices of an arrowhead pattern, in order to be represented as dichotomous matrices. Additionally, the paper employs computational methods to identify the maximum number of ones in certain $4 \times 4$ matrix types in a way that respects the pattern of the matrix.

In a study, researchers examined the elliptical movement of high-energy electrons at a lead-lead collision energy of 5.02 TeV. The analysis focused on electrons generated from the decay of beauty quark particles within specific transverse momentum ranges, as recorded by the ALICE detector. The data was taken from collisions on 11 June 2016. The elliptical movement was observed to vary with transverse momentum and to be similar when comparing beauty quark particles and light charged particles. The results were compared with theoretical predictions based on transport models.

In the study of point clouds, topological methods have gained significant attention. Chromatic alpha complexes, a variant of traditional alpha complexes, use color information to determine which points connect, enabling analysis in multi-colored datasets. This paper explores the topological properties of chromatic alpha complexes, focusing on their homology and the effects of color distribution on topological features. Our findings reveal that the scale-free nature of these complexes, characterized by scale-invariant homology, is influenced more by the relative frequency of colors than by the underlying point distribution. To investigate this, we create synthetic point clouds with varied color assignments and change in dimensionality, allowing us to identify patterns in the persistence diagrams. These diagrams capture the scale-free nature of their topology, where the length of their primary bars is determined by the distance between color classes and their frequency by the relative frequency of the colors involved.

This work investigates the difference in General Degree of Freedom (GDoF) between optimal power control and equal power control in a complex network of K users. It's shown that the GDoG gain of optimal power control over equal power control is proportional to the square root of K, and this result is valid for any number of users K and any possible arrangement of messages. Furthermore, this result holds true in a given subset of networks comprising approximately a quarter of all possible configurations.

Auditing processes often involve categorization tasks, yet existing approaches
lack adaptability.  This research presents adaptable auditing classification
methods grounded in formal concept analysis, formal contextual semigroups, and
the integration of Dempster-Shaft theory, offering two key contributions: (1) a
method for categorizing both existing and new objects, and (2) a solution for
incorporating uncertain information from expert opinions.  This approach is
demonstrated through a practical application in a retail context.

The Strauss process is a point process, and its density is unnormalized relative to a Poisson point process, with the parameter lambda and the radii of disks influencing its distribution. While existing methodologies for sampling from point processes allow for direct sampling in limited spaces, extending this to unbounded domains poses significant challenges, particularly for processes like the Strauss process, whose density diminishes as point configurations move away from the origin. Consequently, sampling on unbounded domains typically involves iteratively refining method-of-rejections samples. In our study, we propose an novel approach that challenges this status-quo by leveraging the fact that restricted Strauss processes have exponentially bounded density. Our proposed method converges much faster than its method-of-rejections counterpart, achieving comparable results in under one second, whereas the method-of-rejections takes over ten seconds.

In this research, we explore the Effect of the Generalized Uncertainty Principle on the key tools used to analyze the Schrödinger equation in the context of Galilean and Lorentz transformations. Our investigation reveals that the standard Galilean transformation tool, based on the wave packet function derived from the Heisenberg relation, becomes inaccurate when considering non-relativistic physics with Generalized Uncertainty Principle. Similarly, when accounting for a length contraction effect based on heuristic arguments, we obtain contradictory outcomes between generalized and standard Lorentz transformations, suggesting an inconsistency. Our findings indicate that the Galilean and Lorentz transformations are not compatible with Generalized Uncertainty Principle.

Multitasking scheduling in service industries has gained significant attention due to workers' ability to perform multiple services concurrently by sharing their skills. Previous research has modeled this problem using parallel machines with setup times, but those studies had limited practical applicability. A new approach has been developed that treats services as machine configurations and models the shared skills as transferable setup times. Various optimization problems have been established, including establishing a optimal schedule for individual tasks and determining the best number of workers required, as well as exploring relationships between different types of optimization problems.

A significant issue in legged locomotion research involves creating strategies for hopping effectively on uneven terrain that can change shape when impacted. This project examines the dynamics of a simple single-leg system that bounces on soft ground, developing a model that accounts for the temporary deformation of the surface during each bounce. Following the established principles of soil mechanics, the development of this system's equations of motion is presented, resulting in a nonlinear mathematical model that simulates the hopping behavior. To further investigate the behavior of this model, a nonlinear simulation is conducted, revealing how variables like the force applied to the ground, the system's energy, and its total height change with each bounce. Additionally, the project involves determining the optimal control strategy that enables the single-leg system to reach a specified target state from a given initial state using the least amount of energy possible. This optimal control problem is solved using GPOPS, yielding the necessary control strategy and energy requirements.

As the number of Internet of Things (IoT) devices continues to expand, especially within smart homes, effective management of these devices becomes increasingly challenging. One critical task involves deploying essential security patches and updating firmware. This process proves particularly difficult in large-scale IoT deployments, especially when dealing with complex wireless network topologies. To overcome these difficulties, researchers proposed the TAU framework, which utilizes an adaptive, multi-device approach, leveraging a series of devices to gradually update the remainder of the network. This proof-of-concept project showcases the effectiveness of the TAU framework, exploring how its design can overcome significant issues associated with IoT deployment. This study investigates various performance aspects, including how user experience is affected by concurrent device updates, the efficiency of TAU compared to conventional methods, and the reliability of large-scale IoT networks during concurrent firmware updates.

We investigated the transition through the many-body localization phase transition, specifically focusing on the behavior of the fock-space propagator, or the participation ratio as a function of system distance. Our study revealed that this propagator follows a power-law behavior for short system sizes and exponential decay for larger systems. We discovered that the localization length associated with the exponential decay scales non-universally near the phase transition point. Furthermore, our analysis shed light on the distinct scaling behaviors of the short and long-system-size regimes, specifically that the power-law regime is multifractal while the exponential decay regime is not. Our results provide a comprehensive picture of the spatial distribution of many-body states and confirm that many-body entanglement exhibits both multifractal and localized characteristics depending on the system size and phase transition regime.

Interactive search models user queries through real-time target identification, 
where a search engine provides visual guidance based on a limited number of cues.
User inputs and system hints form an interdependent cycle of inference and learning.
Traditional visual search models primarily focus on optimizing a single user query by
aiming to minimize the number of required hints. In contrast, we explore a more practical
interactive search framework that accounts for multiple simultaneous targets under a fixed budget 
of hints. Our novel framework, named Regret Interactive Search (RIS), leverages the interplay 
between the number of targets and the allocation of visual hints, and proposes a novel metric 
to evaluate the trade-off between multi-target pursuit performance and budget usage. 
RIS dynamically adjusts the hinting strategy to adapt to varying target counts within a specified 
budget constraint, outperforming existing approaches in both efficiency and accuracy across diverse
datasets.

This study investigates the vulnerability of quantum neural networks (QNNs) to adversarial examples, a major concern for their deployment. An approach is presented for generating universal adversarial perturbations targeting QNNs, a novel concept in this domain. Our results show that a simple foundation circuit in the QNN can become the primary factor in classifying samples with high fidelity under perturbation, a property that can be exploited. Furthermore, we adapt a conventional fast gradient sign method to develop universal perturbations, which we show can be effectively applied across multiple QNN architectures and noise models without requiring access to model internals. Notably, these perturbations significantly decrease QNN classification accuracy in controlled simulations.

We examine Steklov eigenvalues in nearly spherical domains of three dimensions.  Building on our earlier research, we demonstrate the existence of a sequence of Steklov eigenvalue families, each corresponding to the combination of two spherical harmonics of increasingly high degrees.  Within each sequence, the eigenvalues converge to the sum of the Steklov eigenvalues associated with the individual spherical harmonics, and the accompanying eigenspaces converge in the appropriate sense.  The theorems encompass scenarios where the boundary function is smooth ($C^\infty$) as well as cases where it is only Hölder continuous of order $\alpha>1/2$.

Conformance checking focuses on comparing modeled process behavior to observed process behavior from actual event data. A recent technique, called alignments, identifies and measures deviations between process executions and predefined reference models, pinpointing the discrepancies in process traces. Notably, alignments require entire or initial segments of process runs to be exact matches with the reference model, which may not always hold true in real-world scenarios where process runs are only partially observed. These incomplete traces can lead to misleading conclusions about the process's actual behavior. To address this limitation, we introduce new methods known as infix and postfix alignments that can handle unobserved process segments in the middle and at the end of a run respectively. These methods are demonstrated through illustrative examples and formally proven to be effective in conformance checking.

Accurate prediction of radio signal strength in a cellular network is crucial for optimizing performance and ensuring reliability. Traditional methods, such as measurement campaigns, are costly, time-consuming, and impractical for large-scale networks. While stochastic models offer a computationally efficient solution, they often struggle with accurately predicting signal strength. In contrast, deep learning-based models can achieve high prediction accuracy, but currently, there is a lack of thorough evaluation of their real-world capabilities. To address this gap, this paper investigates four deep learning architectures - MLP, CNN, ResNet, and UNet - for predicting RSSI in a real-world scenario. Notably, our approach involves using simulated data to train the models, enabling efficient retraining and testing. Experimental results demonstrate that UNet surpasses other architectures, achieving a mean squared error of 2.5, comparable to the outcome of models trained on actual measurement data.

A straightforward semantics is proposed for temporal planning. We define and formally validate, with formal verification, a validation method for planned actions. This validation operator ensures that actions within a plan are logically consistent and verifiable, based on the semantics we defined. By leveraging the power of Coq, we formally verify the validation operator to guarantee its correctness and reliability.

Power system expansion planning models, used to integrate renewable resources, heavily rely on uncertain input data such as demand and cost forecasts. These models, power flow-based, are sensitive to initial inputs and can produce varying results based on slight input variations. This research explores the impact of uncertainties on model outcomes by analyzing the impact of sample sizes on model results and developing input scenarios to account for energy cost variations. By applying this approach to European power system models, we find that incorporating both distribution and production price uncertainties significantly affects model results, particularly in terms of renewable resource placement. Meanwhile, sample sizes have a lesser impact on results after an initial period. These findings highlight the importance of considering uncertainties in power system models to enhance their robustness.

This study establishes a comprehensive global existence and uniqueness of solutions for the Vlasov-Poisson and the steady Boltzmann-Poisson systems within bounded domains by employing global regularity for the Poisson equation under specific boundary conditions. The study utilizes sophisticated theories from optimal transport and potential theory in its derivation. Furthermore, it meticulously examines various combinations of boundary conditions applicable to both the Vlasov and the Poisson equations to ensure the well-definedness of the problem.

When developers navigate their code, they often utilize search
functionality to find specific items, requiring effective suggestion of
search terms from preceding interactions. Researchers have proposed models
that utilize social signals and language-based features, yet these approaches
demand substantial parameters and extensive training datasets. In this study,
we introduce SLEx, a language-based model that leverages syntactic similarities
to suggest effective search terms, enhancing the efficiency of feature-based
search term suggestions previously explored in literature. By evaluating our
model against baseline and social signal-based methods on two datasets, we
demonstrate its effectiveness in generating optimal search terms. Through
user testing, we demonstrate that SLEx provides valuable search term suggestions
to facilitate concept location.

Researchers have discovered a new class of materials called rheo-acoustic gels through an innovative process that utilizes ultrasound to alter the properties of colloidal gels. This process involves the softening of gels for stress-induced reconstruction and stiffness enhancement. When a sufficiently high ultrasound intensity is applied, it can significantly harden the gel by up to a factor of 10, while also increasing its linear elastic moduli. This application of acoustic energy also leads to significant increases in yield stress, while simultaneously inducing damage to the gel's internal structure, as confirmed through an analysis using x-ray imaging. Interestingly, this acoustic-induced hardening is observed to accelerate as the gel approaches its glass transition point, and these findings are supported by theoretical models derived from the study of lattice dynamics. These remarkable characteristics of rheo-acoustic gels suggest their potential for use in various demanding applications in the fields of engineering and geophysics.

This work offers a novel proof of the Collatz Conjecture, which asserts that every positive integer ultimately generates a repeating sequence of 1 → 4 → 2 → 1 under the Collatz transformation, that is, n → n/2 if n is even, and n → (3n+1) if n is odd.

To effectively process vast amounts of scientific literature, automated system comprehension is crucial. Specifically, domain classification systems rely on accurately identifying the subject matter of each document. This study proposes a new class label prediction system based on Knowledge Graph completion and mathematical entity linking. The proposed system utilizes an educational dataset comprising mathematics and statistics documents and achieves a 62.5% accuracy in automatically linking educational equations within those documents.

In the stable marriage problem, every individual has a set of potential partners ranked by preference, and we're looking for pairings that haven't been rejected by anyone. This pairings issue can be resolved using the Gale-Shapley algorithm through preference lists known to both parties, yet often these lists aren't available and individuals have various choices. In such instances, having ranked lists isn't a strict requirement and individuals can participate in the matching process by accepting or rejecting partners based on their current status and personal desires, ultimately resulting in a matching without instability. This matching process can be likened to an online learning problem, and our paper delves into its implications and limits when individuals have a set of potential partners ranked by preference, and we're looking for a matching that hasn't been rejected by anyone and ranks highest overall, even in instances where ranked lists aren't known. This matching is referred to as the best stable matching, and we've developed a matching algorithm, called LearnMatch, that produces matchings close in quality to the best possible outcome, utilizing a 'Follow-the-Leader' learning technique, and we've shown its effectiveness, even in complex, dynamic settings.

Current evaluation metrics for summarization models have a limitation in that
they are inherently slow due to their dependency on attention models. This
shortcoming is addressed by the proposed SummScore, which achieves a
significant speed improvement over state-of-the-art metrics such as BEQScore.
SummScore utilizes a pre-trained BERT encoder instead, thereby accelerating
inference by 2.5 times while maintaining a high correlation with human scores
(r=0.82) comparable to BEQScore (r=0.83). By employing a special token for
relationship scoring instead of sentence scoring, as done in settings like
dialogue summarization, SummScore overcomes the limitations that arise from
short summary sentences in traditional metrics.

A new technique for extracting signals from "quadratic" data sources is presented. This is achieved by initially transforming the complex data into linear measurements using an innovative method, prior to employing conventional signal recovery methods. The efficacy of this technique is demonstrated in scenarios involving sparse signals recovered via compressed sensing and wideband signals captured by quadratic measurements in radar systems. The effectiveness of this technique is supported by both theoretical analysis and numerical experiments showing accurate signal recovery and resolution of ambiguances.

The incorporation of multiple sensor types in autonomous vehicles has been extensively researched to enhance performance and fault tolerance. Nevertheless, traditional methods focusing on localized features or 3D grid data often neglect the interconnection of features from different perspectives and depend on 2.5D representations that compromise the benefits of 3D data. This work introduces BEVFusion, a lightweight fusion framework that integrates local features with global context to effectively handle multi-sensory data. Diving into the fusion of features from different levels of abstraction, we propose combining higher-level features to boost the robustness and adaptability of our method. Thorough experiments conducted on three benchmark datasets validate the superior performance of our approach, with the source code available at https://github.com/fundamentalvision/BEVFusion.

We have derived an important result that demonstrates how fluid turbulence is influenced by a range of dissipative effects. This result is achieved by applying recent findings from quantum field theory to the stochastic Navier-Stokes equation, which is then compared with direct numerical simulations. In the case of fluids with high Reynolds numbers, the consequences of dissipation at smaller scales are negligible at larger scales. However, in a surprising parallel to a recent discovery in superfluids, the effect of thermal noise causes a significant change in how energy is distributed. In particular, in a certain temperature range, the energy spectrum of a fluid changes from the characteristic -5/3 power law to a thermal equilibrium state, and then transitions to the Kolmogorov -3/3 power law at lower temperatures.

Recent experiments utilizing time-resolved two-dimensional diffraction techniques have allowed researchers to directly observe the thermal profile of a liquid water sample following exposure to a 800 nm, 25 fs pump laser pulse. The experiment involved varying pulse energies between 30 and 120 $\mu$J and a constant 400 nm, 20 $\mu$J probe laser. Researchers observed that the sample's behavior changed from having a confocal focus to a deeper self-focused minimum as the pulse energy increased. Our group developed a novel numerical model, combining the heat equation and optical propagation to calculate the thermal profile and refractive index of the sample with high accuracy, accounting for the effects of heat and density variations on the beam's propagation. The model's results align well with the experiment's findings, validating our approach.

Discussions among developers are increasingly being gathered and analyzed to gain
insights into software systems, their contexts, and related concepts. However,
these discussions contain a range of information structures that can be difficult
to extract consistently. In this study, we investigate the feasibility of using
large language models in a two-step process to mine design-related documentation
from git repositories. Our model demonstrates high accuracy in identifying
designated design discussions and achieves an 85% precision rate. As a result,
our model was applied to transitions in architectural components in Java-based
software systems, where it outperformed alternatives in terms of stability and
reliability, and maintained stability across repeated executions.

This paper presents a new framework, H-STREAM, which enables fast and efficient online analysis of big stream data. The architecture of H-STREAM includes a unified stream interface, and two processing engines tailored for real-time and batch processing. The design of H-STREAM ensures seamless integration of real-time and batch processing through a unified stream interface, and enables efficient processing of big stream data via adaptive processing engines. The evaluation of H-STREAM demonstrates its ability to handle big stream data at scale, and outperforms traditional batch and real-time processing systems.

The theoretical and mathematical underpinnings for top and bottom quark companions are explored within the context of the Minimal Model of Topology (MMT). This analysis involves examining the production of these particles at a proton-proton collider with an energy of 13 TeV. Particular attention is given to non-resonant diagrams for single creation of these particles and calculating their corresponding cross-sections, with a focus on $\tau$-tagging events.

A recent breakthrough in translating English to SPARQL using neural machine translation (NMT) has led to an impressive outcome in retrieving answers from a knowledge base. Nevertheless, this success relies heavily on the specific knowledge base being used during training, and models trained on one KB often struggle to generalize to different knowledge bases, resulting in poor performance when faced with questions involving new KB elements. To tackle this issue, we propose the development of a versatile 'copy mechanism' that significantly improves generalization across various knowledge bases, along with a corresponding data augmentation technique. Experiments conducted on the FBK SPARQL translation dataset reveal the proposed copy mechanism's effectiveness, showcasing up to a 3.9 point relative increase in translation performance on a comprehensive benchmark consisting of 11 datasets.

This research explores the role of venue reputation in predicting citation impact, viewing top scholarly venues as embodying a unique combination of quality indicators. By focusing on venue-level metrics, such as the average citation count per paper from specific venues or venue sets, researchers can more effectively assess new work compared to existing methods. Our study utilizes large-scale datasets to develop robust, non-venue-specific predictors of citation impact for computer science research papers, enabling us to compare different predictor types. Furthermore, our work provides insights into modeling individual venue-specific factors, such as the influence of venue prestige, author affiliations, and topic areas on citation impact.

Advanced learning techniques, including deep learning, have shown remarkable performance in various applications, but their unpredictable behavior makes them unsuitable for use in safety-critical systems. To address this issue, researchers have developed methods for evaluating the reliability of neural networks, with the aim of applying these models in real-world scenarios. This tutorial provides an overview of neural network verification techniques for control systems, covering the modeling of these systems, common prediction and decision verification methods, and the experimental validation of each approach. By exploring the limitations of current verification methods, the tutorial also discusses the promising directions for further research and practical applications.

This study builds upon recent developments in data-driven exploration of complex datasets, specifically functional data clustering. Building on a concept proposed by Sanguineti et al. in 2019, functional clustering is applied to gain a deeper understanding of data structures. Our contributions involve developing novel overlap-based clustering approaches that address two key areas: first, we develop a method to convert any clustering algorithm into one that can handle overlapping clusters, and second, we introduce efficient computational solutions for these new approaches. Focusing on efficient computation, we developed a method that ensures at least linear scalability in terms of the dataset's dimensionality by leveraging a stepwise approach that avoids linear time complexity in terms of the dataset's size. Our proposed approach can be integrated with cutting-edge time series analysis tools such as Dynamic Time Warping and the more dimensionality-reducing Time series Intrinsic Perceptron. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that our solutions perform comparably to state-of-the-art methods, specifically FastCluster, while exhibiting greater flexibility in generating overlapping cluster configurations.

Tensor completion techniques aim to recover incomplete data in high-dimensional tensors generated from various sources. A streamlined tensor ring completion approach significantly reduces computational complexity, yet it remains computationally expensive. This paper introduces a novel streaming algorithm to tackle the problem efficiently. It divides the tensor into consecutive, non-overlapping patches and treats each as an independent low-rank tensor ring for sequential computation. Using patch tracking, our algorithm maintains consistency when predicting the remaining pixels of a patch, allowing for an online reconstruction process. Furthermore, our algorithm can be accelerated by employing GPU parallelization. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our proposed method surpasses conventional methods in recovery quality and exceeds optimized algorithms in processing speed.

It is demonstrated that except in two specific instances, the conjugacy classes within classical Weyl groups have associated Nichols algebras of type BN, where N equals either 4 or 5, all falling under the category of type-oriented standard pairs. This finding is part of a broader theorem that establishes, given a standard pair (G1, G2), if the Nichols algebra related to a reflection representation of G2 is finite, its bicrossed product with that of G1 will also have a finite Nichols algebra over the resulting reflection representation, provided the bicrossed product itself exists.

Three-dimensional rotating turbulence, occurring at very high rotation rates, is characterized by inertial waves whose motion is controlled by the Rossby number, which is much less than one. In such a scenario, wave interactions become nonlinear and may result in an energy cascade that follows a specific power-law spectrum, first hypothesized by Hallberg and Richardson in 2001. By conducting large-scale direct numerical simulations, we compared theories and simulations and found a clear match between simulated spectra and theoretical predictions, specifically a(k) proportional to k^(-10/3), thereby confirming a key prediction of inertial wave turbulence theory.

For graphs where each edge has an associated positive value representing its weight, I investigate the link between two different maximum weight independent sets in the graph, N-GISET-G, and N-GISET, which differ in that the latter involves normalizing the weights of repeated values before performing the computation. I demonstrate that for graphs where each edge has a associated positive value representing its weight, the difference in set size between N-GISET-G and N-GISET is at most one. Furthermore, I show that if an edge weight meets this criterion, its normalization results in a difference of at most two, while for graphs without normalization of edge weights, the set sizes of N-GISET-G and N-GISET are equal approximately 75% of the time.

This research study examines the impact of a magnetic field and electric dipole on electrically modulated single-layer graphene, aiming to investigate its specific heat and other thermodynamic properties. A general solution is achieved in a parabolic band structure with modifications brought about by the interaction between the magnetic field and electric dipole. Parity transformation symmetry breaking occurs due to electric modulation, which influences velocity and acceleration in a one-dimensional free electron system. Specifically, electron acceleration is directly proportional to the magnetic field strength and electric dipole intensity. Additionally, heat capacity exhibits oscillations corresponding to both the magnetic field strength and electric modulation.

M-dwarf star binaries, which emit low-frequency radio waves, hold the key to understanding the origin and nature of this type of radio emission. A comprehensive analysis of the 11-year monitoring of the cataclysmic variable system, white dwarf and M0.8 V secondary in binary CR Draconis, revealed continuous, low-frequency radio emission originating from the secondary star. Spectral analysis indicated electron-cyclotron maser emission linked to the secondary star's magnetic activity and rapid rotation. Observations showed that the emitted radio waves vary in intensity and polarization, consistent with a rotating magnetic dipole model, and the polarization changes are due to the star's rotation axis not being aligned with its orbital axis. Moreover, the research suggests that the gap in magnetic flux required for electron-cyclotron maser emission could be formed due to the star's interaction with its companion's magnetic field.

By combining traditional photorealistic rendering techniques with learning-based approaches, virtual avatars can be generated from a single input image, showcasing remarkable progress. Current research has utilized neural volume rendering and pre-trained neural networks to synthesize realistic avatars. Nonetheless, creating dynamic 3D representations of articulated avatars remains a significant challenge. An existing method, which relies on latent variable optimization, has demonstrated success on simple tasks, yet it struggles to produce high-quality results on articulated avatars due to the complexity of the task and the inefficiencies of the optimization process. In our research, we introduce Articulated Neural Rendering (ANR), a framework designed to obtain high-quality, articulated avatar rendering results from simple models and 3D model annotations. To address optimization issues, ANR employs neural implicit surfaces and a novel rendering pipeline. Our experiments reveal that ANR surpasses prior work on avatar rendering tasks, demonstrating improved visual quality, the ability to utilize much smaller model parameter sets and achieve remarkable 360-degree, articulated avatar rendering results.

Recent advances in artificial intelligence, particularly in computer vision, have been significant, with state-of-the-art models now rivaling and often exceeding human abilities. However, the susceptibility of these models to manipulation by computer-generated adversarial examples remains a concern. A novel type of adversarial example has emerged, involving an image with a simple, unnatural transformation that deceives an AI model into incorrectly categorizing it, while a human would easily recognize its true identity. In contrast, a newly discovered class of adversarial examples known as Human Adversarial ExamplesHAIs are images that have been altered by a human to deceive both AI models and human observers into incorrectly categorizing them. A contrasting type, known as Human Adversarial Examples Unique to HumansHAUOs, are images that humans can easily deceive an AI model through, while other humans cannot. In an experiment involving collaborations with humans, it was found that extreme image transformations have different effects on humans and machines, with humans generally being less vulnerable to deception in comparison.

The connection between the Askey-Wilson algebra and both the SU(2) Chern-Simons theory, along with its associated quantum group, has been established and formalized. Specifically, a construction has been found for a conformal block that is also a weight 3 Vassiliev invariant within a key 3-manifold, with the Vassiliev invariant being linked to the Askey-Wilson algebra. Furthermore, it was discovered through a rescaling of a quantum Racah-Wigner symbol that the flat link algebra is indeed a form of the Askey-Wilson algebra.

Our study involves a cluster quantum Monte Carlo examination of the thermodynamic properties of frustrated antiferromagnets on a two-dimensional trimer cluster lattice at large but not infinitely large spin values. We discovered a spinon continuum within the spinon gauge theory framework for weakly-coupled lattices, which is not present in the spin-charge separation theory. We investigated how the system transitions from a trimer cluster to a cluster glass state and how this transition behaves in relation to the system's spin value. Additionally, our results indicate that the system undergoes a smooth quantum phase transition from a paramagnetic to a cluster glass state as the system's spin value decreases below 2. We observed that the system exhibits a finite temperature phase transition from a cluster spin fluid state to a cluster glass state at extremely low spin values.

Pre-trained language models (PLMs) have been utilized to facilitate zero-shot learning utilizing the embeddings of class definitions as class identifiers. However, current approaches often rely on a single class definition per category, lacking diversity in wording, structure, and scope. To address this limitation, our study employs multiple class definitions per category to create a richer set of embeddings for each class. Achieving this, our research focuses on two key aspects: diversifying class definitions through adapting existing PLMs and expanding these definitions by generating new ones. Specifically, our findings demonstrate that fine-tuning language models like BERT on a large dataset of definitions, such as Wikipedia, can yield definitions that are both semantically related to the class and structurally comparable to one another. Additionally, our study explores zero-shot learning using GPT-2 to generate multiple class definitions, which when combined with meta-tuning, results in state-of-the-art performance on various benchmarks, surpassing previous methods by approximately 2%.

In-depth research into a specific three-dimensional invariant version of the next-generation non-minimal supersymmetric standard model is conducted, focusing particularly on first-order electroweak phase transitions and their connections to gravitational wave detection, along with the'split' scenario's non-minimal model, linking the model's characteristics to the formation of gravitational waves during the first-order phase transition.

We thoroughly examine the interplay between several aspects related to gravitational waves and charge parity odd properties within the non-minimal model, within the context of dark matter investigations and results from the Large Hadron Collider.

We have successfully identified two three-dimensional invariant non-minimal models featuring rich CP-violating behavior, where one model's dark matter candidate is lighter than $100\ GeV$ and the other is between $100$ and $120\ GeV$.

We have identified two three-dimensional invariant NMSSMs with first-order phase transitions, exhibiting a significant radiative symmetry breaking and featuring stable, baryon-candidate dark matter.

We have identified a region in parameter space for gravitational wave detection, specifically between $10^{-3}$ and $10^{-2}$ for a specific model's three-dimensional invariant model $\lambda$, which could potentially be observable by LISA in the future.

We have identified another region in parameter space for gravitational wave detection, specifically between $10^{-1}$ and $10^{3}$ GeV for a specific model's three-dimensional

We introduce novel techniques for automatically detecting and validating
human-solving strategies in Sudoku. Leveraging this, we created a 'High-z
Sudoku' game to systematically explore 'Submm Sudoku', a new approach for
identifying reliable redshifts from compact spectra. A database of
10 million Submm Sudoku was developed, encompassing high-z galaxies with weak
ALMA spectra and known redshifts from other methods, including optical, near-IR,
or mm-wave spectra. Our analysis revealed a success rate of 70-80% on high-
quality spectra, with an even higher rate on lower-quality data. Moreover, our
error analysis suggests that Submm Sudoku's redshift estimation errors are
generally smaller than those from standard redshift estimation methods. Our
near-infrared spectral database, comprising ~1000 high-z galaxies, was analyzed
using Submm Sudoku and demonstrated a success rate of approximately 75%,
comparable to conventional redshift estimation methods. Our study highlights the
significance of binary decision trees in assessing the reliability of any
algorithmic solution.

This study uses time-resolved two-dimensional exchange spectroscopy to examine the spin-lattice correlation function of a Heisenberg antiferromagnetic triangular lattice of cuprates. Contrasting the results with a previous Raman study that proposed dynamic signs of an incompressible spin liquid phase, our data supports a picture in which an incompressible spin liquid and other ordered phases coexist within the triangle-bonding regime. Specifically, our findings reveal a $3q$-like fluctuation that diminishes with increasing temperature and a unique long-lived excitation at frequencies of 2.5 and 3.5 terahertz, indicative of a spin-3 excitation arising from an incompressible spin liquid where spins experience an effective triangular lattice of exchanges.

This study investigates the phase transitions occurring between confinement and deconfinement within $SU(3)-$Higgs theory, revealing a complex relationship between these states. While in the presence of an $U(1)$ factor this theory exhibits two distinct phases, this research demonstrates that $SU(3)-$Higgs theory undergos a single, unique confinement-deconfinement transition, which does not necessarily coincide with the phase transition observed in the complex case. Furthermore, the phase transition occurring here is not necessarily confined in both the spatial and temporal dimensions. Beyond this, critical points within the phase diagram are studied in greater depth. Specifically, this research explores the behavior of non-Abelian electric flux, Wilson loops, and string tension, which serve as key indicators of confinement. Numerical simulations of the model, involving both spatial and temporal compactifications, are conducted, which reveal a trispectrum of critical points within the phase diagram. These results are then compared with the analogous $SU(3)-$Higgs model, which includes an additional $U(1)$ factor.

Cr2Al, a newly identified antiferromagnetic intermetallic compound, exhibits a
unique magnetic behavior that can be precisely measured through neutron
experiments, revealing the in-plane magnetic structure and its temperature
dependent variations. These results challenge the initial understanding of the
magnetic properties of Al-based Heusler compounds, suggesting an additional
type of magnetic interaction is significant in smaller ferromagnetic variants.
Our research indicates that three distinct types of magnetic interactions need to
be accounted for when modeling the system using the symmetry of the Noopur Noori
magnetic group at room temperature, with a primary interaction contributing
about 90% to the magnetic properties, but taking on different characteristics
at lower temperatures, beyond its high-temperature behavior. These outcomes
align with both the results of first-principles calculations and earlier
experiments involving the related compound, Mn2Al.

A new kinetic model is developed for rare gas under the influence of thermal nonequilibrium conditions, incorporating an expression for collision frequency that varies with particle velocity. This analytical expression was originally proposed by the authors in previous work. The proposed kinetic model is mathematically similar to the well-known monatomic gas kinetic model of Shakhov. The impact of an expression for collision frequency that depends on velocity, influencing transport properties in rare gas gas under thermal nonequilibrium conditions, is evaluated. The expression for collision frequency that depends on velocity is mathematically solved within the Shakhov approximation. The resulting kinetic model of Shakhov type, derived from the expression for collision frequency that depends on velocity, is mathematically similar to the Shakhov model. The new kinetic model is tested using numerical simulations of two fundamental problems, including plane Couette flow and Poiseuille flow with thermal nonequilibrium conditions.

One key challenge in moving from data-driven semantic parsing approaches to methods that require minimal human labeling but substantial data, these two methods often coexist in real-world applications. A proposed solution, naturalized semantic parsing, utilizes language models to generate input texts aligned with logical forms that can be trained on. A new, solver-based approach to naturalized semantic parsing was developed, which achieves significant accuracy improvements and can be trained on much smaller datasets, this new method was demonstrated to achieve comparable results with a subset of the data, this new method was successfully applied to a dataset of grammatical agreement, which required training on only 5% of the available data, this new method was shown to be more scalable and efficient than previously explored neural approaches.

The Electron-Ion Collider's future will involve utilizing electron-proton and electron-nucleus collisions to thoroughly analyze the proton and nucleus internal structures through detailed measurements. Achieving precise results relies heavily on measuring forward jets with high accuracy in fractions of light, small fractions, and pinpoint locations. Optimizing a specialized forward silicon tracker's design for this purpose is being carried out by collaborating groups to support the future EIC's scientific objectives.

The star-forming galaxy NGC 4466 hosts a low-mass active galactic nucleus with a disc-like structure that has been the subject of significant debate.  By analyzing light curves across multiple bands, we discovered that the nucleus undergoes large fluctuations in brightness, varying by up to 1 magnitude over the course of days.  These variations, which are visible in both optical and near-infrared light, cannot be attributed to short-term variability in accretion processes, as they have timescales that are too long.  Rather, our findings suggest that these variations may be due to either large-scale eruptions or low-frequency oscillations in the nucleus, which could provide valuable insights into the physical conditions of the disc, even in relatively faint AGN, which are otherwise challenging to study.

Our comprehensive study of the magnetic field configuration of HD58260, a magnetic Ap-type star with an unusually low surface field strength, involved a meticulous, line-by-line analysis of 20 lines exhibiting both absorption and emission lines that are sensitive to the Lande factor. The analysis, which combined high-resolution, line-by-line synthetic spectra and non-LTE line formation models tailored to each line, allowed us to derive a precise, line-by-line map of the stellar surface magnetic field. The results challenge the prevailing notion that non-emitting lines provide the most accurate measurements of the average Lande factor. In contrast, our research reveals that emission lines offer a distinct advantage in accurately mapping the star's surface magnetic field. The observed discrepancies can be attributed to the complex interplay between the star's strong magnetic field and its atmosphere, which alters the energy levels of the upper levels of certain lines. The study underscores the necessity for precise, line-specific modeling to accurately interpret both emission and absorption lines sensitive to magnetic fields.

A link exists between a Dunkl operator over a field with two elements and a first derivative, 
exemplified through its equivalence to an operator comprising two first derivatives in the same field.

A recent discovery has highlighted the potential of the 8.8 micrometer fine structure line, specifically H30$\alpha$ at 1.865 THz, as a reliable tracer of star formation in young massive stars. This research assesses the effectiveness of the H30$\alpha$ line in mapping star formation within the young massive star cluster region SFR1 in NGC 5253. The data obtained from the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array reveals the presence of H30$\alpha$ emission, which is consistent with the theories of star formation. The measured H30$\alpha$ flux suggests a star formation rate of approximately 0.04 to 0.06 solar masses per year. The spectral analysis of H30$\alpha$ indicates a minimal amount of continuum dust emission and a moderate amount of ionized gas. The spectral energy distribution analysis of the H30$\alpha$ emission suggests the presence of a moderate amount of dust extinction. The spectral analysis of H30$\alpha$ also shows no significant variation with distance from the center of the emission, which is consistent with the theories of star formation. The spectral measurements of H30$\alpha$ are compared to other spectral lines, such as [OIII] 88 micrometer and CO lines, to understand the physical conditions of the emission. We demonstrate that two continuous minimal actions of the infinite dihedral group on an infinite compact Hausdorff space can be orbit equivalent but not conjugate even when considering actions on the Bohr compactification. Consequently, the previously established rigidity of virtually cyclic group actions no longer holds, and we also show that the same notion is not stable under a 2-blanking equivalence relation for such actions on the Bohr compactification.

We analyze the $L^2$ approximation of conditional expectation operators on a finite-dimensional space. The operators are defined with respect to a random variable's distribution and we derive a new concept, the best linear operator, which does not require specific parameterizations. Its existence and uniqueness are proven under certain conditions on a generating set. The approximation's accuracy is quantified by its characterization in terms of the distribution's properties. A specific application involving the epsilon-machine representation of chaotic processes is discussed, supported by numerical results. The research has potential implications for characterizing Markovianity in such systems.

Designing effective state observers for nonlinear systems, such as the spread of infectious diseases, is crucial for implementing optimal control strategies. This study focuses on developing state observers for epidemic models, using a novel approach based on Liapunov equations, which offers improved convergence rates. The proposed method can be applied to generalized SEIR processes, and its efficiency is验证ed through comprehensive modeling and simulation of an observational dataset from a specific region in Spain during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Recent studies have shown that using position-based information in a temporal knowledge graph as additional data for learning node embeddings significantly improves performance in making predictions. Nevertheless, the impact of incorporating this information has not been thoroughly examined. This study investigates the effectiveness of employing a pre-trained, unadjusted static model that disregards the multihop relationships within the graph as a static framework for integrating this information, and evaluates its performance against various deep learning models. Our results demonstrate that the proposed static model that utilizes precomputed node embeddings yields satisfactory results and the added benefits of incorporating the temporal dimension are quite negligible. Our findings also reveal that the performance of deep learning models that utilize node embeddings derived from dynamic, time-dependent processes is not necessarily superior to that of the static model that utilizes this information as a static framework for integrating the position-based information within the graph.

Research into Kerr-lens mode-locking (KLMD) for ultrafast oscillators has long been a priority due to its potential for generating high-energy pulses. Recent advancements in this field have been hindered by a lack of a thorough understanding of this technique's fundamental principles. This knowledge gap has led to an over-reliance on a single explanation, which is now insufficient for explaining KLMD-based oscillators capable of producing high-power pulses. A new study aims to address this issue by developing a general mathematical framework for KLMD. A crucial discovery in this research is the identification of a new, more accurate method for analyzing the stability of lasers exhibiting KLMD. This method, based on geometric optics, is more versatile and can be applied to a broader range of KLMD-based lasers. A further analysis of this research reveals that a particular lens placed within the cavity is responsible for the Kerr-lens effect, and its position and strength can be used to predict the behavior of KLMD. A new design for KLMD-based lasers is also proposed, which relies on this internal lens to optimize the cavity's performance. A model is also developed to provide a more accurate description of pulse formation in these lasers. A further study of this research reveals that a particular lens placed within the cavity is responsible for the Kerr-lens effect, and its position and strength can be used to predict the behavior of KLMD.
